items.title: Declarations of Pecuniary Interest under the “Municipal Conflict of Interest Act”
Laura Hamilton and Marion Thomson Howell, A Better Tent City
notes:
L. Hamilton and M. Thomson Howell expressed support for the report CSD-HOU-25-010 staff recommendation. L. Hamilton provided a brief overview of the impact of Better Tent City and expressed appreciate for funding provided by the Region. M. Thomson explained the importance of additional support to ensure that the property is secure and safe. She requested that the Region increase the recommended funding support by $180,000 which would be used to pay for full time dedicated security staff that would assist residents to ensure safety and organization of the community.

In response the Committee, L. Hamilton explained that there is a focus for transitioning residents to permanent housing and several residents are waiting for permanent affordable housing. Since April 2020, transitioned 36 residents to permanent housing and there are additional residents ready to transition, however, they are unable to connect with permanent housing. She confirmed that there are only a maximum of 42 cabins and that amount cannot be expanded.

Responding to Committee, M. Thomson Howell explained that on September 1, 2025 there was a visitor reset to ensure that only residents were on-site. Better Tent City staff are looking for opportunities to restart visitor access, however, there are several considerations prior to resuming access such as resources and security. M. Thomson Howell further confirmed that the site was fenced off since December 2024.

notes:

items.title: CSD-HOU-25-011, Waterloo Region Housing Revitalization Plan – Remaining Redevelopment Projects
notes:
P. Sweeney and R. Pettipiere provided context for the Waterloo Region Housing Revitalization Plan – Remaining Redevelopment Projects. R. Pettipiere noted that the Revitalization plan has been in place for five years and he noted the housing landscape has changed significantly over the past five years. These changes have presented various challenges as staff work toward completing the three final housing revitalization projects at Mooregate Cresent, Courtland-Shelley, and 140 Weber Street. The staff recommendation proposes next steps for these projects while balancing community need for affordable housing and fiscal responsibilities. He highlighted that staff are recommending delaying the Mooregate project by one year in order to determine capital and debt costs. He further highlighted that both the Courtland-Shelley and 140 Weber Street projects be delayed until 2030 in order to establish business cases for both the development and operating models and incorporate these projects into the capital plan.

Responding to the Committee, R. Pettipiere stated that number of individuals or families on the Region housing waitlist is approximately 11,000 and the list grows approximately 5-15% annually and that the growth has been exponential. He explained the tenant relocation program for both the Mooregate site and the Courtland-Shelley site. He confirmed that the all tenants at the Mooregate site, which had 55 units, have been relocated. He further confirmed that the relocation of tenants at the Courtland-Shelley site has begun and is approximately 50% complete.

M. Rodrigues presented a motion for the Committee to consider as it relates to the Housing Revitalization Plan.

In response to the Committee, R. Pettipiere confirmed that staff will review the Build Canada Homes funding program once the details have been released. He cautioned that this funding could jeopardize other federal funding for sites such as Mooregate. P. Sweeney further confirmed that staff believe the presented motion is feasible and the delay of a project for a year will not address debt servicing and will look for various modelling options including partnership opportunities.

The Committee expressed support for the Committee motion and the work of Community Services.

P. Sweeney confirmed that the project at Mooregate is shovel ready and is a community-driven project that has strong partnerships. 

Responding to a question related to budget. Nicole Neil, Director of Corporate Services, explained that all departments conducted rigorous review of their budgets to achieve the less than 5% tax increase. 

P. Wolf disagreed with Community Services programs undergoing any budget reduction as there are lifesaving considerations.

motions.item_title: CSD-HOU-25-011, Waterloo Region Housing Revitalization Plan – Remaining Redevelopment Projects
motions.text: That the Regional Municipality of Waterloo direct the Commissioner of Community Services and Commissioner of Corporate Services to report to the Community and Health Services Committee by the end of Q1 2026 to: Identify and bring forward all viable funding and financing opportunities, including but not limited to re-prioritizing other regional projects to achieve long-term debt sustainability principles, to advance construction of Mooregate within one year, as identified in CSD-HOU-25-011; and Provide an update to report CSD-HOU-24-021, dated December 3, 2024, where Council directed staff to explore affordable housing development partnership opportunities with the non-profit and private sectors that create enhanced or additional long-term affordable housing units, are beneficial for existing tenants, or produce cost-sharing outcomes, as well as to present a plan to advance site and development readiness in the interim prior to construction.
motions.text_html:
That the Regional Municipality of Waterloo direct the Commissioner of Community Services and Commissioner of Corporate Services to report to the Community and Health Services Committee by the end of Q1 2026 to:

  1. Identify and bring forward all viable funding and financing opportunities, including but not limited to re-prioritizing other regional projects to achieve long-term debt sustainability principles, to advance construction of Mooregate within one year, as identified in CSD-HOU-25-011; and
  2. Provide an update to report CSD-HOU-24-021, dated December 3, 2024, where Council directed staff to explore affordable housing development partnership opportunities with the non-profit and private sectors that create enhanced or additional long-term affordable housing units, are beneficial for existing tenants, or produce cost-sharing outcomes, as well as to present a plan to advance site and development readiness in the interim prior to construction.
